newsitem.title: JORDAN: Banking gains lift Amman bourse in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Banking gains lift Amman bourse in busy trade.

text.p: Strong banking sector gains helped lift the Amman bourse by nearly half a percent on Monday in busy trade.
Brokers said local demand helped push up Bank of Jordan by 0.15 dinars to 3.37 dinars in Monday's busiest turnover, worth 364,000 dinars ($513,000).
Arab Bank also rose by one dinar to 255 dinars in busy trade. Brokers said non-Jordanian Arab investors were taking an interest.
"Overall the volume was good, boosted mainly by the banks," said Ibrahim Odeh of Wataniyeh Financial Services.
Seven of the 10 banking shares traded on Monday rose, pushing the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index up 0.41 percent to 159.97 points in healthy turnover of 1.04 million dinars.
But Jordan National Bank fell slightly to 2.12 dinars, despite having attracted international demand recently.

Brokers say the bourse is generally stable amid growing foreign interest which resurfaced since Saturday and could signal the start of a repeat pattern of select bargain buying on cement and mining firms which the bourse witnessed last month.
"Maybe the foreign buying will start up in the next few days," Odeh said.
Prices have eased since gaining nearly six percent in the final week of May on the back of foreign fund buying.
Jordan Cement, which has been targeted by foreign investors, rose 0.05 dinars to 4.08 dinars and
Overall rising shares outnumbered losers on Monday by 19 to 10, with another 13 trading but closing unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.24 percent to 81.43 points, 2.36 percent down from the start of the year. -- Amman newsroom +9626 623776
